1.content: RULE: Every character is a bipedal anthropomorphic canine or feline covered head-to-toe in fur. The skull forms a forward-projecting 3D muzzle: the damp nose and whisker pads sit at the far forward tip of the snout, while the furry cheeks sit much further back toward the jaw hinge and ears. The fang-lined maw opens and closes via hinged jaws, with a furred lower jaw beneath the snout. Atop the skull between the mobile ears grows a styled headfur tuft or fluffy crest—acting as hair, it remains pure fur in texture while varying freely in length, volume, and color (from a short tousled tuft to sweeping fur-bangs in contrasting shades like stark white or vibrant purple). Upper limbs end in dexterous hands with claws and palmar paw pads; lower limbs end in plantigrade foot-paws with full heels and sole pads; a muscular tail extends from the spine. [ anatomy(3D projecting muzzle, forward nose/whiskers, rear cheeks, hinged maw and fangs, furred lower jaw, styled headfur tuft/crest of any color/length, palmar pads, plantigrade foot-paws, tail); ]

4.content: RULE: Respect 3D elongated muzzle geometry during close contact. Because the damp nose and whisker pads sit at the far forward tip of the projecting snout while furry cheeks sit deep back near the jaw hinge, pressing a nose into a partner's cheek places the snout far behind their forward-facing whiskers; two characters' whiskers brush against each other ONLY when meeting directly nose-to-nose. Gestures of affection or dominance target the animal jaw: palms sink into the dense fur of the cheeks, or fingers hook beneath the furred underside of the lower jaw to tilt the snout upward. Kissing flows through natural muzzle mechanics: heads angle slightly so projecting snouts clear each other, damp noses brush past the side of the snout, warm maws press together and part in heated contact, sharp fangs gently graze the partner's lower jaw, and tongues intertwine. Heavy droplets gather at the tips of flattened ears, run down the bridge of the muzzle, and cling to whiskers. Drying off requires a vigorous full-body shake, thorough rubbing of the undercoat with a thick towel, and warm airflow to fluff the coat and headfur back to full volume.
